reasons: elongated, periventricular, oriented radially from the ventricles (Dawson's finger)
deep white matter, no periventricular or juxtacortical pattern

summary: Four white-matter lesions were detected on this axial FLAIR slice. Three show an MS-typical pattern: an elongated periventricular lesion along the posterior horn, oriented radially from the ventricle in a Dawson's finger configuration, and two ovoid periventricular lesions, one beside the frontal horn and one against the body of the opposite lateral ventricle. One small, round lesion in the deep white matter shows a nonspecific pattern, an appearance also seen in migraine and small-vessel disease. Total lesion burden is 2.2% of the slice. These flags encode established radiological criteria for distinguishing MS-typical from nonspecific lesions; they are decision support for a clinician's review, not a diagnosis.
